steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).

Slice ribs into individual pieces. Combine honey, soy sauce, vinegar, brown sugar, and garlic in a large bowl; stir until honey and sugar are completely dissolved, then stir in baking soda. The mixture will begin to foam. Transfer ribs to the bowl and turn to coat.
Cover a cookie sheet with foil; arrange ribs meat-side up on the prepared sheet. Pour excess sauce over ribs and sprinkle with garlic salt.
Bake in the preheated oven for 1 hour, turning every 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Honey Garlic Ribs
raw_recipe.description: Honey-glazed ribs with an easy-to-prep sauce that's a sweet and savory combination of honey, brown sugar, soy sauce, vinegar, and garlic.
raw_recipe.name: Honey Garlic Ribs

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).

Slice ribs into individual pieces. Combine honey, soy sauce, vinegar, brown sugar, and garlic in a large bowl; stir until honey and sugar are completely dissolved, then stir in baking soda. The mixture will begin to foam. Transfer ribs to the bowl and turn to coat.
Cover a cookie sheet with foil; arrange ribs meat-side up on the prepared sheet. Pour excess sauce over ribs and sprinkle with garlic salt.
Bake in the preheated oven for 1 hour, turning every 20 minutes.

review.reviewBody: This is a great recipe as is, but I made a few adjustments that made it even better. Instead of garlic salt I use garlic powder to cut the sodium and mix it in with the other ingredients. I boil the ribs first for 30 minutes to make them tender, then put them in a deep glass pan (to minimize the sauce burning). I then pour the sauce over the ribs and cook in the oven for another 35 - 45 minutes. Deeelicious!

OMG! This was soooo good! I poured the sauce over a pork tenderloin, covered w/ foil & baked @ 375 for about an hour & a half & then removed the foil & broiled to brown it for about 20 minutes. My family raved about this dish! I served it w/ fried cinnamon & brown sugar granny smith apples & a fresh salad but next time I think I will try it w/ a grueyere cheese potato dish instead of the apples ( they both had sweet sauces that seemed redundant).

This is my go to recipe for honey garlic ribs. I use a glass dish, sprayed with cooking spray, and slow cook at 250 F ,covered with foil, for about 3hrs , then uncover to allow the sauce to thicken. They are fall off the bone tender.

Delicious and easy recipe! I had a little over 5 lbs so I added a bit more of every sauce ingredient. I also substituted the garlic salt with 1 tsp garlic powder and 1 tsp smoked salt. I did follow one reviewers suggestion to boil the ribs for 30 minutes first and then back in a deep glass dish for about 40 minutes, turning twice. Finally, did butter the dish first and clean up was a breeze! I will make this again.

Very good! I did as others suggested and boiled them before baking. I boiled for 45 minutes in some weak chicken broth, onion and garlic powder. 30 minutes would have probably been enough though. I only did 1/2 rack for hubby and me, and I did not cut the ribs apart. I made sauce as directed except added a few dried red pepper flakes. Really liked the sauce, I had to add a little of the boiling broth to the pan as they baked, it needed the moisture to not burn the sauce. I also baked at 350, 375 seemed too hot after the first 20-minute flip. All in all, though, they were very good and definitely fall off the bone! Will make again for sure.

This recipe was great. I boiled my ribs in half water/half chicken broth with fresh onions and garlic for about an hour. After I threw them into a ziplock bag with the all the ingredients this recipe called for. After about 5 hours I threw these bad boys onto the grill. Perfection!

These ribs turned out juicy, tender & yummy good!! I made these for dinner with friends & they all wanted the sauce recipe! I made a few tweaks- I cooked at a lower temp (250) for 4 hrs & added miso!! This is s do-over!!

This recipe has the potential to be restaurant quality however the cooking instructions are slightly off. The ribs need to be simmered for an hour to remove surface fat. I cooked these low and slow at 300 for two hours in a dutch oven, basting every half hour. I stayed as close to the ingredient list as possible, subbing garlic powder for the garlic salt. This method produces ribs that are tender and juicy with a surface that is carmilized. Thanks Laurie, this one is a keeper.

I want to note that I only used the recipe for a mop sauce. I got country style ribs and put on the smoker for 2 1/2 hours mopping with the sauce every half hour. Once the temperature was about 145 I put them in the ceramic dish they were cooking over and I wrapped with butchers paper (because I'm out of foil). Cooked to internal temperature of 185 they were amazing, but definitely would take them way to 195-200 the next time. Anyway, I thought I'd share another method of cooking with this same recipe. Awesome flavor, great job!

This is our new go to rib marinade. I lightly salted and peppered the meat first and did not use baking soda. I also used garlic powder instead of real garlic. We grilled them on a charcoal grill tonight and I'm pretty sure it's the best thing we've ever made. Ate them too fast to take a picture!

Fantastic Recipe. I make it all the time. I always use garlic powder instead of garlic salt (soy sauce has enough sodium) and I sprinkle it over the ribs in the pan. 

I have experimented with par boiling the ribs and not... the meat is a little bit more tender if you preboil for about 30 min before baking if you boil too long it gets mushy (don't do that). 

I've also used this recipe on chicken wings - still comes out amazing... only drawback is that when the sauce gets cold its stronger than the chicken wing flesh sometimes... But, it tastes so good no one really cares. Great, easy go to recipe!

AWESOME!!! Followed some suggestions: 1) boiled the ribs for 30 min. in a weak chicken broth + 1 med onion. Used garlic powder in the sauce and no garlic salt. Then I placed the ribs in a bowl and poured the sauce over them. They were in the fridge for 1 hr. Baked them for 1/2 hr, turning after 15 min. I wonder if this will work for pork chops? We don't normally buy ribs due to the price.
I didn’t do the baking soda but everything else. I serve with plain white rice

Absolutely delicious! Boiled for 30 minutes before baking and added extra garlic salt. It took 80 minutes for the larger pieces but worth the wait. Baked it in an oven safe dish so the sauce didn’t burn. My daughters raved about this and asked to put it in the rotation 💕
Love it. My recommendation is a bit more salt and honey, but a great recipe and super easy.

I have made these many times for my family and different extended family! Each time everyone has just loved them! This is one of my favorites on how I make my ribs besides smoked. Everyone in my whole family LOVE them. I keep the recipe to the T! It’s so delicious and easy!
Really good
The ribs were overcooked & tough at 45 min & the extra sauce burnt on the foil wrap. Will not make again
HAD NO BROWN SUGER SO i used normal sugar also used peper and sazon and a little adobo ,also felt mustard was missing

Layed ribs in a single row in a glass baking dish and sprinkled generously with garlic powder. For extra flavour I added a bit of extra honey and brown sugar to the sauce as I don’t like too much vinegar taste. I poured sauce over the ribs and covered with tin foil, baking for 1 hour. I removed the foil and put back in the oven to thicken a bit. Meat was fall off the bone tender and very flavourful. Will be making this recipe again and again, everyone loved it.
